title: Map reusable MW2 host code to concrete MW3 component boundaries
goal: Apply the owner's request to maximize compatible reuse from PaulCombal/mw2-recompiled by identifying existing reuse and concrete C++/tool candidates at exact source identities, without repeating failed whole-runtime adaptation or adding unused copied code.
acceptance: Verify the current public upstream revision against the existing pin and license identity; distinguish root project licensing from third-party/generated/game/SDK and binary-distribution rights

Inspect and hash representative C++ host utilities, configuration/diagnostics, input/audio/files, renderer/cache/prewarm, analysis/toolchain and networking/security/install components; record actual dependencies, disposition and the MW3 seam or task needed before each adoption

Identify existing disc-reader adaptation and private MW2-derived host-tool use accurately; preserve tested MW3 runtime/layout/termination failures without treating them as a rejection of all independent MW2 code

Publish a prioritized, actionable reuse manifest and report that prefer compatible upstream implementations when a real MW3 consumer exists; retain notices, MW3 executable identity, bounded tests and separate shared-interface scope for actual ports

Keep source inspection separate from executed integration/performance evidence; change no runtime/SDK, guest addresses, main-lane reservation, renderer choice, service gate, launcher or production service
validation: Reconcile each recorded file hash and source link with the clean pinned checkout, current upstream HEAD and root license; validate unique component IDs and referenced MW3 tasks/paths
Run python tools/check.py and metadata/diff/provenance checks; no new parser/runtime execution, game benchmark, GPU suite or external service claim follows from this research-only change
Record owner self-review or actual independent review, explicit unresolved provenance/integration limits and evidence required for each subsequent scoped port
size: bounded source-reuse inventory and adoption priorities; actual component ports remain independently scoped implementations
